definitions.explanation: Doing something while showing resistance or lack of enthusiasm. Implies going along with something despite not wanting to.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧しぶしぶ⟦{承諾|しょうだく}した→承諾する：18993_shoudakusuru⟧。
しぶしぶ⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧しぶしぶ⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: The child reluctantly started their homework.

notes:
MIMETIC ORIGIN:
Reduplicated form related to ⟦{渋|しぶ}い→渋い：06820_shibui⟧ (astringent, reluctant). The repetition emphasizes the reluctance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- しぶしぶ⟦{承諾|しょうだく}する→承諾する：18993_shoudakusuru⟧ - to agree reluctantly
- しぶしぶ⟦{従|したが}う→従う：02059_shitagau⟧ - to comply unwillingly
- しぶしぶ⟦{受|う}け{入|い}れる→受け入れる：05755_ukeireru⟧ - to accept grudgingly
- しぶしぶ⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ - albeit reluctantly

POSITION IN SENTENCE:
Appears before the verb, modifying the manner of action.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{嫌々|いやいや}→嫌々：07795_iyaiya⟧ - unwillingly (stronger negative feeling)
- ⟦{仕方|しかた}なく→仕方ない：11434_shikatanai⟧ - having no choice
- {渋々|しぶしぶ} - alternative kanji spelling
